lesson.title: Saturday Point #3
lesson.hook: Your serve at 30–40, built from five more of your lessons. Two choices each shot: the one you want to hit, and the one that wins.
lesson.memHTML: Serve it up high. Step in, make space, keep it low.
lesson.tomorrow: In your next match, on a second serve, aim deep with kick, then look for their high, short reply and step in.

steps.name: Break point down
steps.q: Where does your second serve go?
opts: Safe, into the middle of the box
steps.payoff: Deep with kick reaches them above the shoulder.
steps.principle: In is only the beginning. Judge a second serve by the contact it gives them.
steps.why: The safe serve lands in but sits up at chest height, so they step in and attack. Deep with kick climbs above their shoulder and their return is weak.

lines.A: It sits up chest high. They step in and attack; you're stretched.
lines.B: Right: it climbs above their shoulder.

steps.name: High and short
steps.sit: Their return floats back high and short.
opts: Move in and take it early
Stay back and take it at the top
steps.payoff: Moving in meets it at your waist, before it climbs.
steps.principle: A short high ball can be met early. Take it before it climbs.
steps.why: Staying back, it reaches you above the shoulder and you can only float it back. Moving in, you meet it at waist height and drive it deep.
steps.take: High and short? Move in and take it early.

lines.A: Right: waist high, and you drive it deep.
lines.B: Above your shoulder: you float it back, and you're stretched.

steps.name: Low and slow
steps.sit: They slice it back low and slow, into your backhand half.
steps.payoff: The slow slice buys the time to set up your bigger weapon.
steps.principle: Use the bigger weapon when you have time to set it up.
steps.why: A low, slow slice gives you time. The backhand only keeps the rally neutral; running around puts your forehand on a ball you can attack.
steps.take: Slow slice to your backhand? Run around it.

lines.A: Safe, but it's just a neutral rally ball. You're in time.
lines.B: Right: there's time to get round it.

steps.name: Getting round it
steps.sit: You're getting round it for the forehand.
opts: One big step to the ball
steps.payoff: Space at contact is what lets you swing through.
steps.principle: Check the space at contact first.
steps.why: One big step lands you on top of the ball: crowded, the swing comes off short and slow, and they attack it. Small steps leave room to drive it deep.
steps.take: Last steps? Small ones. Leave space.

lines.A: Right: space to swing. Deep crosscourt, and they chip and charge.
lines.B: Crowded: it comes off short and slow, and they attack it.

steps.name: They come in
steps.sit: They chip it and come in, stopping around the service line.
steps.payoff: At the service line, a ball at their feet makes them volley up.
steps.principle: Read where they stop. At the service line: their feet.
steps.why: Stopping at the service line, they have time to cover a lob and put it away. A dipping ball at their feet makes them volley up, and you pass the floater.
steps.take: Net rusher at the service line? Their feet.

lines.A: From the service line they get to the lob and volley it away.
lines.B: Right: they volley up, and you pass them.
